title: Polynomial lift and Laurent residue stratum of a formal monoid chart
statement:
Let $L$ be a field or a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_L$, and let $S,T$ be sharp fine saturated additive monoids [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], sharp meaning that $0$ is the only invertible element. Let $K$ be a finite free abelian group, $P=K\oplus T$, and $f:S\to P$ a homomorphism $f(s)=(\delta(s),\beta(s))$ such that $\beta(s)\ne0$ for $s\ne0$. Fix $n\ge0$, write $t=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$, and set
$$R_0=L[S][t],\quad I=(\mathfrak m_L,[s]:s\ne0,t)R_0,\quad H_S=\varprojlim_jR_0/I^j,$$
$$E=L[K][t],\quad U=L[P][t]=E[T],\quad W=H_S\otimes_{R_0}U.$$
Completions and tensor products use [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; the $R_0$-algebra map to $U$ sends $[s]$ to $[\delta(s)][\beta(s)]$ and fixes $L,t$. Monoid rings $E[M]$ consist of finite sums $\sum c_u[u]$ with $[u][v]=[u+v]$.
Then $I$ is finitely generated, $R_0,U,H_S,W$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and there is an isomorphism
$$W\cong H_S\otimes_{\mathbf Z[S]}\mathbf Z[P]$$
sending $x\otimes l[p]t^e$ to $xlt^e\otimes[p]$ and $x\otimes[p]$ back to $x\otimes[p]$. In particular $W/IW\cong U/IU$ by the canonical map.
For any prime $\mathfrak n$ of $W$ containing the images of $\mathfrak m_L,t$ and every $[v]$ with $v\ne0$ in $T$, put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak n\cap E$ and $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak n\cap U$. Then
$$\mathfrak p\supset(\mathfrak m_L,t),\quad\mathfrak r=\mathfrak pU+([v]:v\ne0),\quad IU\subset\mathfrak r,$$
and $\mathfrak n$ is the unique prime over $\mathfrak r$ containing $IW$. The residue field maps give
$$\kappa(\mathfrak n)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak r)\cong\operatorname{Frac}(E/\mathfrak p)$$
with residue fields and localizations as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. In the Cohen case, every $\theta\in H_S$ satisfying $\theta-p\in([s]:s\ne0,t)H_S$, where $p$ generates $\mathfrak m_L$, maps into $\mathfrak n$; the residue field of $(W/(\theta))_{\mathfrak n/(\theta)}$ is the same field.

source.place: VI 1.6, printed p. 70; agent-supplied polynomial coefficient lift and residue-stratum calculation, returned proof Steps 6--7.

proof.text: A field has only the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$; a Cohen ring is a principal ideal domain by [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Thus $L$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Choose finite nonzero monoid generators $s_1,\ldots,s_a$ of $S$, generators $v_1,\ldots,v_b$ of $T$, and a basis $k_1,\ldots,k_c$ of $K$. Finite generation of the monoids is part of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Any nonzero $s\in S$ has a generator in an expression as a sum, so $[s]$ is divisible by some $[s_i]$. Hence $I$ is generated by $\mathfrak m_L$ (zero or principal), the $[s_i]$, and the $t_j$. The monomials $[s_i]$ and $t_j$ generate $R_0$ as an $L$-algebra; $[\pm k_i]$, $[v_h]$ and $t_j$ generate $U$ as an $L$-algebra. Sending variables to these finitely many elements gives surjections from finite polynomial rings. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to obtain that $R_0$ and $U$ are Noetherian.

source.place: Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence) and 00FM (section-Noetherian); finite monoid-generator calculation for the models of ILO VI 1.6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] to the Noetherian ring $R_0$ and its ideal $I$ to obtain Noetherianity of $H_S$. As an $R_0$-algebra, $U$ is generated by the same finite list $[\pm k_i],[v_h]$: $L$ and all $t_j$ already come from $R_0$. Every tensor in $W$ is a finite sum of $x\otimes u$, and expressing $u$ as a polynomial in that list shows that $W$ is generated over $H_S$ by $1\otimes[\pm k_i],1\otimes[v_h]$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] applied over $H_S$ proves that $W$ is Noetherian.

Write $V=H_S\otimes_{\mathbf Z[S]}\mathbf Z[P]$. Define $W\to V$ on finite sums by $x\otimes l[p]t^e\mapsto xlt^e\otimes[p]$, and $V\to W$ by $x\otimes[p]\mapsto x\otimes[p]$, extending additively. The first formula is balanced over $R_0$: moving $l$ or $t_j$ between factors has the displayed effect, while moving $[s]$ is precisely the relation $x[s]\otimes[p]=x\otimes[f(s)+p]$ in $V$. The second is balanced over $\mathbf Z[S]$ by the same relation in $W$. These checks and bilinearity define the maps by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Multiplication agrees on monomials since $[p][q]=[p+q]$ and $t^et^d=t^{e+d}$, and then on finite sums by distributivity. Both preserve $1$. The composites are the identity on $x\otimes[p]$ and $x\otimes l[p]t^e$, respectively, because $l,t^e$ can be moved across the $R_0$-tensor. These tensors additively generate, proving the asserted ring isomorphism.

source.place: VI 1.6, printed p. 70: agent-supplied polynomial coefficient lift, explicit balanced maps.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] with $A=R_0$, the finitely generated ideal $I$ of Step 1 and $N=1$, the first-coordinate map induces an $R_0$-algebra isomorphism $H_S/IH_S\cong R_0/I$. Let $\bar x$ be the image of $x$ under this map. The balanced map $x\otimes u\mapsto\bar x\bar u$ defines $W\to U/IU$ and kills $IW$; here $\bar x$ acts through $R_0/I\to U/IU$. Conversely $u\mapsto1\otimes u$ modulo $IW$ kills $IU$. These two ring maps are inverse: for each $x$ choose $a\in R_0$ lifting $\bar x$, so $x-a\in IH_S$ and $x\otimes u\equiv1\otimes au\pmod{IW}$. On the $U$ side the composite fixes every $u$. Hence the canonical $U$-algebra map $U/IU\to W/IW$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), N=1; explicit tensor quotient inverse.

proof.text: Put $J=([v]:v\in T\setminus\{0\})U$. Sharpness implies that $v+w=0$ in $T$ forces $v=w=0$, since either summand would otherwise be invertible. Therefore constant coefficient in the $T$-basis defines a ring retraction $\epsilon:E[T]\to E$ with kernel exactly $J$: an element of the kernel is its finite sum of nonzero-monomial terms. By hypothesis $J\subset\mathfrak r$. For every $u\in U$, $u-\epsilon(u)\in J$, so $u\in\mathfrak r$ iff $\epsilon(u)\in\mathfrak p=\mathfrak r\cap E$. This proves $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak pU+J$ and $U/\mathfrak r\cong E/\mathfrak p$. Contraction of the given prime also gives $\mathfrak p\supset(\mathfrak m_L,t)$. Finally every generator of $I$ maps into $\mathfrak r$: this is already true for $\mathfrak m_L,t$, and for $[s]$ with $s\ne0$ it follows from $[s]\mapsto[\delta(s)][\beta(s)]$ and $\beta(s)\ne0$. Hence $IU\subset\mathfrak r$.

source.place: VI 1.6, printed p. 70: agent-supplied calculation of the closed monoid stratum by constant coefficients.

proof.text: The same generator calculation shows $IW\subset\mathfrak n$. The isomorphism in Step 4 commutes with the maps from $U$. Consequently primes of $W$ containing $IW$ are inverse images of primes of $U/IU$: explicitly, given a prime $\mathfrak a\supset IU$ of $U$, take the inverse image in $W$ of $\mathfrak a/IU$ under $W\to W/IW\cong U/IU$. Its contraction to $U$ is $\mathfrak a$, and it is the only such ideal, since the quotient map is onto. Taking $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak r$ proves the asserted uniqueness of $\mathfrak n$ and yields the canonical isomorphism $W/\mathfrak n\cong U/\mathfrak r$.

source.place: VI 1.6, printed p. 70: agent-supplied prime calculation from the explicit quotient isomorphism.

proof.text: For a ring $A$ and a prime $\mathfrak a$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] with $I=\mathfrak a$ and the zero prime of $A/\mathfrak a$. It identifies $A_{\mathfrak a}/\mathfrak aA_{\mathfrak a}=\kappa(\mathfrak a)$ of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] with the localization of the domain $A/\mathfrak a$ at all its nonzero elements, namely $\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak a)$. On fractions it sends the residue class of $a/s$ to $\bar a/\bar s$. Use this for $(W,\mathfrak n)$ and $(U,\mathfrak r)$ and then the quotient isomorphisms of Steps 5--6. They give $\kappa(\mathfrak n)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak r)\cong\operatorname{Frac}(E/\mathfrak p)$. The first is induced by $U\to W$: its map on domain quotients is exactly the inverse of $W/\mathfrak n\cong U/\mathfrak r$. Thus these are the specified residue field maps, not just abstract field isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), applied with I equal to the prime; definitions of localization and residue field in Tags 00CO and 07BH.

proof.text: In the Cohen case the hypothesis on $\theta$ expresses $\theta-p$ as a finite sum of $H_S$-multiples of positive $S$-monomials and the $t_j$. Their images lie in $\mathfrak n$, as does $p\in\mathfrak m_L$, so $\theta\in\mathfrak n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] with $A=W$, $I=(\theta)$ and prime $\mathfrak n/(\theta)$. It gives $(W/(\theta))_{\mathfrak n/(\theta)}\cong W_{\mathfrak n}/\theta W_{\mathfrak n}$. Its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak nW_{\mathfrak n}/\theta W_{\mathfrak n}$: an element outside it lifts to a unit of $W_{\mathfrak n}$. Quotienting by that maximal ideal gives $W_{\mathfrak n}/\mathfrak nW_{\mathfrak n}$, since $\theta\in\mathfrak n$. This is $\kappa(\mathfrak n)$, the field identified in Step 7.
